title: First Rain
paragraphs: Kai had seen Earth every single day of his life, but only ever through glass. From the observation deck of Crescent Base, it hung in the black sky like a marble streaked with blue and white, so close that he sometimes felt he could reach out and pluck it from the darkness. Home, for Kai, was a string of domes and tunnels half buried in grey dust. The air was pumped in, the temperature never changed, and the only plants were lettuces, growing in tidy rows under purple lamps.

Now, at the age of eleven, he was going to Earth for the first time, to meet Gran. For months, he had exercised on a treadmill with heavy weights strapped to his ankles, because the doctors had warned him that Earth's gravity was six times stronger than the Moon's. Even so, when the shuttle landed after its three-day journey and Kai tried to stand, he gasped. His arms and legs felt as though they had been filled with wet sand, and his head seemed far too heavy for his neck.

But the gravity was not the worst part. When the doors of the spaceport slid open, Kai stopped dead. Above him there was no dome and no ceiling: just a vast, pale-blue emptiness that stretched on for ever. His hand flew to his throat, feeling for the seal of a helmet that was not there. At home, an opening to the sky meant only one thing. Alarms would wail, emergency doors would slam shut, and the precious air would come rushing out into space. 'It's all right,' Mum said gently, taking his hand. 'The air here doesn't go anywhere. The whole planet holds it down.' Kai nodded, but all the way to Gran's cottage he kept his eyes fixed firmly on the ground.

Gran lived at the edge of a village, where the lane ran out and the fields began. She was smaller than she looked on the video screen, and she hugged him very carefully, as if he might break. That night, Kai lay awake in a narrow bed under a sloping ceiling, listening. On the Moon, the only sound at night was the steady hum of the air machines. Here, everything seemed to have something to say: the wind whispered in the chimney, an owl hooted somewhere in the darkness, and a dog barked on a distant farm.

The next morning, Gran led him out into the garden. The grass was cool and damp beneath his bare feet, and Kai crouched down to run his fingers through it, amazed that nobody had planted it in rows. A small brown bird hopped along the fence, watching him with its head on one side. On Earth, it seemed, things were simply allowed to grow wherever they liked.

Then the sky began to change. Clouds the colour of wet slate rolled over the hills, the light grew dim, and a strange, fresh smell rose from the earth. Something cold struck Kai's cheek, then his arm, then the top of his head. He looked up in alarm and saw water falling out of the sky: thousands upon thousands of drops, pattering on the leaves and drumming on the roof of the shed. On the Moon, every drop of water was measured, cleaned and used again, and wasting it was the worst thing anyone could do. 'Gran!' he yelled. 'The sky's leaking!'
Gran laughed so much that she had to hold on to the fence. 'That's rain, love,' she said, when she could speak again. 'It's meant to do that.'

Kai stood very still. He had read about rain and watched films of it, but nothing had told him how it would feel: soft and cool, tapping on his skin like a thousand tiny fingers. He tipped back his head, closed his eyes and let it run down his face. When Mum came out with an umbrella, he shook his head. By the time they went inside, he was soaked to the skin and grinning from ear to ear.

That night, Kai sent a message to his best friend, Dev, back at Crescent Base. He tried to describe the grass, the birdsong and the enormous sky, but none of the words seemed big enough. In the end, he deleted everything and wrote just one line: 'You have to come and see it for yourself.'

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 1.
Which **two** things does the writer tell us about Kai's home on the Moon?
Tick two.
options: The air was pumped in.
Flowers grew in every room.
The temperature never changed.
It was built beside a lake.

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 2.
When Kai tried to stand, what did his arms and legs feel as though they had been filled with?

Look at paragraph 3.
Why did Kai's hand fly to his throat?
Tick one.
options: He had a sore throat after the long journey.
He was used to an open sky meaning danger, so he reached for a helmet.
He was trying not to shout with excitement.
He wanted to take off his helmet to breathe the fresh air.

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 3.
'the **precious** air would come rushing out into space'
Which word is closest in meaning to **precious**?
Tick one.
options: valuable
fresh
invisible
noisy

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 4.
'everything seemed to have something to say'
What does the writer suggest with these words?
Tick one.
options: The animals on Earth could talk to Kai.
Kai could hear many different sounds, unlike on the quiet Moon base.
Gran talked to Kai for most of the night.
The village was completely silent.

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 6.
Find and copy **one** word that shows Kai was frightened when he looked up.

Look at paragraph 8.
The rain was 'tapping on his skin like a thousand tiny fingers'.
What does this tell you about how the rain felt to Kai?
questions.model: It felt soft and gentle, like lots of light little touches, and it was pleasant rather than frightening.
points: explaining that the rain felt gentle, soft or light, like lots of tiny touches, or that it felt pleasant.
Do not accept answers saying that the rain hurt or was heavy.

questions.prompt: Using information from the text, tick one box in each row to show whether each statement is **true** or **false**.
statements: The journey from the Moon to Earth took three weeks.
Gran lived at the edge of a village.
The clouds that rolled over the hills were the colour of wet slate.
Kai used the umbrella that Mum brought out.

questions.prompt: Using the whole text, give **two** ways in which life on the Moon base is different from life on Earth.
questions.model: On the Moon base, the air is pumped in and an opening to the sky is an emergency, but on Earth 'The whole planet holds it down'. Also, on the Moon the only plants are lettuces growing in tidy rows under purple lamps, but on Earth grass grows wherever it likes.
points: each difference that makes clear what is different in the two places (1 mark each), such as:
air: on the Moon it is pumped in and an opening to the sky lets it rush out; on Earth the planet holds it down
plants: on the Moon only lettuces grow, in rows under purple lamps; on Earth grass grows wherever it likes
sounds at night: on the Moon there is only the hum of the air machines; on Earth there are wind, owls and dogs
water: on the Moon every drop is measured, cleaned and used again; on Earth rain falls from the sky
the sky: on the Moon Kai lives in domes and tunnels; on Earth there is a vast open sky
gravity: Earth's gravity is six times stronger, so Kai feels heavy

questions.prompt:
Look at paragraph 9.
Why do you think Kai deleted everything and wrote just one line?
Explain fully, using evidence from the text.
questions.model: Kai could not describe Earth properly, because 'none of the words seemed big enough'. He had learned for himself that reading about rain and watching films of it was not the same as being there, because 'nothing had told him how it would feel'. Earth had amazed him so much that he wanted his best friend to experience it too, so he told Dev, 'You have to come and see it for yourself.'
points: Explains that Kai could not find the words to describe Earth, e.g. 'none of the words seemed big enough'.
Explains that Kai has learned that reading or watching films is not the same as being there, e.g. 'nothing had told him how it would feel'.
Explains that Kai wants Dev to experience Earth for himself, because it has amazed him so much.

questions.prompt:
Do you think Kai will want to visit Earth again?
Use evidence from the text to support your prediction.
questions.model: Yes. I think he will want to come back, because by the end of the story he loves Earth. He let the rain run down his face and was 'grinning from ear to ear', he was amazed by the grass, and he tells Dev, 'You have to come and see it for yourself.' He might even bring Dev with him next time.
points: a prediction (1 mark), e.g. yes, he will want to come back; he will want to bring Dev with him.
evidence from the text that supports the prediction (1 mark), e.g. he was 'grinning from ear to ear' in the rain; he refused the umbrella; he tells Dev, 'You have to come and see it for yourself'.
A 'no' answer can score only if it is backed up with evidence, e.g. Earth's gravity made his arms and legs feel as though they 'had been filled with wet sand'.

questions.prompt:
Which is the best summary of the whole story?
Tick one.
options: A family leaves Earth to start a new life on the Moon.
A boy who has grown up on the Moon visits Earth for the first time and is amazed by it.
A boy on the Moon base mends a broken air machine.
A boy visits Gran on the Moon and helps her to grow lettuces.

questions.prompt: Number these events 1 to 5 in the order they happen in the story.
items: Kai lets the rain run down his face.
Kai hears an owl hooting in the darkness.
Kai exercises with weights strapped to his ankles.
Kai sends a message to Dev.
Kai feels for a helmet that is not there.
